title: Origami workspace weave: compact navigation and contextual switchboard for rollouts & cost views
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Problem statement: The current Redwood Console navigation has grown organically: multiple lanes (left rail, top nav, command palette) contain overlapping targets (dashboards, rollout controls, cost breakdowns). This causes discoverability regressions for new users and cognitive load for platform teams. Goal: design a compact, role-aware navigation weave that surfaces rollout controls and cost views with low friction, preserves keyboard-first workflows, and supports canary/A-B rollout tasks without adding noise to focused flows.

Scope: redesign of sidebar/rail + workspace switcher interactions, route affordances for rollouts and cost dashboards, prototypes for compact vs expanded states, and implementation guidance for Console engineering and PMs (interaction specs, responsive rules, telemetry hooks). Excludes backend rollout orchestration and billing APIs (engineering to own).

Success metrics: improved discoverability (user test task completion +20%), reduced time-to-open cost dashboard (median < 3 clicks), fewer mistaken navigation clicks to rollout controls in prod support sessions, and developer adoption of the compact nav within Dedicated customers pilot.
acceptance_criteria: New nav presents workspace switcher and role-aware quick actions in <= 2 visual taps for 90% of tested workflows
Cost breakdown links available as persistent, contextual hub from model/route pages
Rollout controls accessible from route-level header and global rail without exposing advanced options by default
Keyboard-first command palette integration preserves existing shortcuts and introduces focused compound commands (e.g., 'Open workspace X > Open rollouts')
Prototype validated with 6 PM/Eng/design reviewers and usability test N=12 with engineers and platform PMs
decisions: Use a single compact left rail by default, with progressive expansion on hover and explicit 'pin' state
Expose concise rollout affordance (status chip + CTA) on route headers; move advanced rollout controls behind a modal to avoid accidental changes
Workspace switcher becomes a lightweight typeahead with recent/role-aware suggestions and a persistent 'Manage workspaces' link
Surface cost insights as a contextual drawer from the model/route header and as a global 'Cost' hub in the rail; default view shows high-level units (tokens, latency cost) with quick filters
Keyboard-first interactions are primary: preserve Cmd/Ctrl+K and introduce Cmd+Shift+P to open 'Quick workspace actions'
Accessibility: ensure 4.5:1 contrast for all nav icons and labels, full keyboard navigation, and ARIA live regions for rollout status changes
tradeoffs_considered: Compact rail reduces surface area but increases hover-discovery dependence—mitigated via explicit pin and command palette coverage
Moving advanced rollout controls into modals reduces accidental edits but requires careful focus management and autosave warnings
Contextual cost drawer increases discoverability but risks cluttering the route header; chosen to keep header lightweight and use transient drawer instead
engineering_notes: Requires route metadata endpoints to expose 'can_view_rollouts' and cost-telemetry pointers
Telemetry hooks required: nav_open, workspace_switch, rollout_modal_open, cost_drawer_open, cost_filter_apply
Recommend feature flag gated rollout of new nav per-org for a 2-week canary before wide release
CSS strategy: use utility-first tokens and a collapsed rail sprite to minimize repaint cost on hover transitions
reviews: 2025-03-03 - PM review by Anika Bose: emphasized faster access to cost per-model; requested a persistent cost link in global rail
2025-03-04 - Eng review by Malik Henderson: flagged need for route metadata endpoint and cautioned about hover animation cost on low-end GPUs
2025-03-05 - Accessibility review by Priya Nair: requested ARIA attributes for rollout modal and keyboard trap tests
2025-03-06 - Design critique with Clara Nguyen and Tomas Becker: approved compact rail visuals but asked for stronger affordances for pinned state
user_testing: Prototype sessions (N=12) conducted 2025-03-01..2025-03-04: engineers completed 'open cost for model X' task in median 2.1 clicks (baseline 4.3)
Qualitative feedback: 8/12 liked quick workspace typeahead; 3/12 requested clearer separation between global cost hub and per-route cost drawer
Edge case observed: users with >50 workspaces wanted grouping and favorite pins; we added 'starred workspaces' to backlog
open_questions: Should cost drawer show estimated dollar values by default or keep tokens/latency as primary metrics?
What guardrails should we include for rollback actions exposed from the quick rollout affordance?
Do platform admins need a 'force pin nav for workspace' org setting?
How to present rollouts for multi-model routes where a route references more than one served model?
next_steps: Finalize Figma screens for pinned vs unpinned states by 2025-03-10
Align with Backend on route metadata API and feature flag plan (EPIC: ENG-5302) by 2025-03-12
Add 'starred workspaces' microstory to backlog and estimate in next planning cycle
Prepare canary rollout plan and telemetry dashboard queries for experiment tracking
